answer: The voyage multiplier is published, charged in wharf, and comet lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2727 identities would post 1256 proofs and burn roughly 51 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
